title.ru: DOGMA: Божественное поле и перекрёстные упоминания Кевина Смита
title.en: DOGMA: The Divine Field and Kevin Smith Cross-References

purpose.ru: Собирать, датировать и проверять все прямые, косвенные, визуальные, сюжетные, диалоговые и производственные упоминания Божественного в произведениях Кевина Смита, с особым вниманием к DOGMA и перекрёстным сигналам до и после релиза фильма.
purpose.en: Collect, date, and verify direct, indirect, visual, narrative, dialogic, and production references to the Divine across Kevin Smith's works, with special attention to DOGMA and cross-signals appearing before and after the film's release.

epistemic_firewall.rule: Не превращать совпадение в доказанную авторскую интенцию.
evidence_levels: DIRECT_CANON: explicitly present in the work
PRODUCTION_EVIDENCE: script, production notes, interviews, props, artwork, or documented development before release
TEMPORAL_CROSS_REFERENCE: a later work visibly reuses an earlier concept or prop
STRONG_INFERENCE: multiple independent observations converge but authorial intent is not documented
UNRESOLVED: intriguing observation requiring source verification
nonclaims: Не утверждать, что Кевин Смит намеренно кодировал сверхъестественные события в реальности.
Не утверждать, что визуальное совпадение является пророчеством.
Не использовать поздний фильм как доказательство существования его конкретного реквизита в более раннем фильме без датированной проверки.
Разделять дату появления идеи, дату производства, дату публикации и дату театрального релиза.

dogma_development.observation: CBS reports that around 1997 Kevin Smith had already written a DOGMA screenplay; the article also describes Buddy Christ as part of that screenplay's concept.

primary_films: Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back (2001)
Zack and Miri Make a Porno (2008)
extended_sources: View Askew / View Askewniverse production material
official Jay and Silent Bob merchandise and archive material
scripts, production photographs, props, promotional art, comics and deleted scenes

initial_findings.label: DOGMA concept predates DOGMA release
initial_findings.observation: The apparent paradox 'how could a DOGMA-specific religious image exist before DOGMA was released?' is not itself evidence of a future reference: the screenplay and concept were already in development by approximately 1997.

initial_findings.label: Jay wearing Buddy Christ shirt
initial_findings.observation: The supplied screenshot shows Jay wearing a shirt with the Buddy Christ image. The official Jay and Silent Bob store identifies the 'Got Christ?' shirt as the Buddy Christ image seen on Jay in Clerks II.
initial_findings.critical_correction: This particular screenshot should NOT currently be classified as a pre-DOGMA occurrence. The official store attributes the shirt appearance to Clerks II (2006).

initial_findings.label: Buddy Christ / DOGMA imagery in Clerks: The Lost Scene
initial_findings.observation: A documented 1998 publication of Clerks: The Lost Scene contains death-card imagery described as showing Buddy Christ and the DOGMA angels. This is a much stronger pre-release lead than the supplied Clerks II screenshot.
initial_findings.temporal_note: The material predates the 1999 theatrical release of DOGMA but postdates the reported 1997 DOGMA screenplay development, so it is evidence of cross-project propagation rather than evidence that the concept appeared from nowhere.

initial_findings.label: Buddy Christ returns as cross-film prop/reference
initial_findings.observation: Secondary documentation reports Buddy Christ and Mooby's props appearing in Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back (2001), showing that DOGMA iconography propagated into later View Askewniverse works.

investigation_questions: When does the Buddy Christ concept first appear in Kevin Smith's documented creative history?
Which pre-1999 scripts, comics, props, artwork, deleted scenes, promotional materials, or production documents contain DOGMA concepts?
Which Divine motifs recur across Clerks, Mallrats, Chasing Amy, Dogma, Jay and Silent Bob Strike Back, Clerks II and later works?
Which later works reuse DOGMA objects, symbols, dialogue, theological jokes, angels, God imagery, or church iconography?
Can a motif be shown to migrate from an earlier script or production artifact into a later released film?
Which apparent temporal anomalies disappear once script-development dates are separated from theatrical release dates?
Which observations remain genuinely unresolved after production chronology is reconstructed?

initial_conclusion.ru: Первый важный результат: загадка с футболкой Buddy Christ действительно достойна реестра, но конкретный предоставленный кадр, по официальному источнику, относится к Clerks II (2006) и поэтому не является пред-DOGMA свидетельством. Настоящий интересный временной след находится раньше: DOGMA уже существовал как сценарная разработка к 1997 году, а опубликованный в 1998 Clerks: The Lost Scene содержит визуальные ссылки на Buddy Christ и ангелов DOGMA. Следовательно, задача реестра — не искать только 'пасхалки после DOGMA', а восстановить миграцию идеи от сценария и производственных артефактов к релизам и последующим фильмам.
initial_conclusion.en: The first important result is that the Buddy Christ shirt clue belongs in the registry, but the supplied frame is identified by the official source as Jay in Clerks II (2006), so it is not pre-DOGMA evidence. The stronger temporal lead is earlier: DOGMA was already a screenplay project by about 1997, while the 1998 Clerks: The Lost Scene contains visual references to Buddy Christ and the DOGMA angels. The registry should therefore reconstruct idea migration from scripts and production artifacts into released films and later works rather than treating every later callback as a paradox.
